quotes.quote: NPCI/UPI/OC-226A/2026-27 — 03rd July 2026 To, All UPI Member Issuer Banks, PSP Banks and UPI Applications Dear Sir/Madam, **Subject: Enhancement of Transaction Limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication in UPI** Reference is drawn to NPCI circular NPCI/UPI/OC-226/2025-26 dated 07th October 2025, wherein On-Device Biometric Authentication (Fingerprint, Face, etc) was introduced as an additional option for authentication in lieu of UPI PIN. In view of increasing adoption in the ecosystem, it has been decided to revise the per-transaction limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication (fingerprint, face, etc.) in UPI is hereby enhanced from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, effective 07th August 2026. Issuer Banks, PSP Banks and UPI Applications to ensure adequate customer communication regarding the updated limit. All existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable, and participants are required to ensure adherence. Yours faithfully, SD/- Sourabh Tomar Deputy Chief UPI Product

findings.reason: The answer cites S8 and S9 to describe reconciliation checks. However, S16.1 (from document 128, a predecessor addendum) explicitly states that acquirer banks must reverse transactions through credit adjustments on the same day or T+1, while S13.1 and S14.1 from Circular 17 mandate daily reconciliation of GL accounts for all UPI transactions. The answer does not clarify whether the 'three-way reconciliation' in S9 supersedes the specific reversal timelines in S16.1 or the general daily GL reconciliation in S13.1/S14.1, creating a potential conflict between specific operational timelines and general reconciliation requirements.
